traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Yucca brevifolia (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.43 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 2 records in 2 sources); trunks 0.43, branches 0.46. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The National Park Service's Joshua Tree National Park page (read): Joshua trees typically flower for the first time at about 50 to 70 years of age, or around 2.5 m tall. The Woody Plant Seed Manual's 5 to 6 years (Yucca, read) is for the genus under favourable conditions. The rosette program's own flower_age, a crown's age, stays; the period is for the checks.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tree 3 to 12 m tall whose trunk and branches carry dense rosettes of stiff, dagger-like, finely toothed leaves 15 to 35 cm long; a branch tip that flowers, or is damaged, stops and two or three branches grow from below it, so old trees branch every 0.6 to 0.9 m of growth (FEIS); dead leaves cling to the branches as a shaggy skirt; flowering is irregular, in good years only. Not fitted to measurements. The stem's radius under a rosette (0.05 m, a branch about a quarter as wide as its rosette, which FEIS gives as 0.3 to 0.5 m) and how gently a branch turns back up (upturn 0.05, so that inner branches stand erect and outer ones spread level, as FEIS describes) were set by eye against iNaturalist photographs (imagekit), 2026-10-27; with upturn 0.5 every branch turned upright into a candelabra.

generator.params.dead_angle.note: FEIS Yucca brevifolia (read 2026-10-27): "Dead leaves are persistent and fold down, covering the branches and coating the trunks of young trees". A dead leaf hangs 15 degrees off the stem, along it; the angle is set by eye against iNaturalist photographs (imagekit), 2026-10-27. At 150 the dead leaves stood out from the branches like a brush.

generator.params.dead_life.note: No count of the years a dead leaf hangs was found. FEIS says the dead leaves coat the trunks of young trees and are shed from old trunks, which then show their bark. 25 years, about a metre of branch under a rosette, set by eye against iNaturalist photographs (imagekit), 2026-10-27. At 40 years, the dead leaves covered whole branches.

generator.params.old_angle.note: FEIS gives the leaves (15 to 35 cm by 0.7 to 1.5 cm, with a spine 7 to 12 mm at the tip) but not their angle. A rosette's oldest leaves open past level, to 105 degrees from the stem, so a rosette is a ball as in the iNaturalist photographs (imagekit), set by eye 2026-10-27. At 60 a rosette was an upright tuft.

appearance.bark_pattern.note: FEIS Yucca brevifolia (read 2026-10-27): the bark or periderm is "soft and cork like"; "Bark plates measure 3 to 6 inches (7.5-15 cm) long by 1 to 2 inches (2.5-5 cm) in thickness". Plated bark whose plates are 10 cm long (scale 0.04 times elongation 2.5), the middle of that range, standing deep (depth 0.5) for their thickness. Their width round the stem, the fissures and the contrast were set by eye against iNaturalist photographs (imagekit), 2026-10-27.

appearance.twig.note: FEIS Yucca brevifolia (read 2026-10-27): dead leaves "fold down, covering the branches", and leaves have enlarged bases where they attach to the branch. A young branch, under 5 cm in radius, is drawn in the grey-tan of its leaf bases and thatch, which hide its wood, turning to the bark's colour by 15 cm. The colour and the radius were set by eye against iNaturalist photographs (imagekit), 2026-10-27.

generator.params.trunk_rate.note: FEIS Yucca brevifolia (Gucker 2006, read): unbranched seedlings grew about 7.6 cm a year for their first 10 years and about 3.8 cm a year after; 21-year-old unbranched trees averaged 5.9 cm a year. The rate after the first ten years, most of a tree's life, is taken.

generator.params.fork_length.note: FEIS Yucca brevifolia (read): branches form after the terminal bud dies from flowering or insect damage, and fork at 0.6 to 0.9 m (2 to 3 ft) intervals. A branch may fork once it has grown 0.6 m.

generator.params.fork_spread.note: FEIS Yucca brevifolia (read): branches fork at 0.6 to 0.9 m intervals; 0.3 m between the two ends.

generator.params.girth_rate.note: FEIS Yucca brevifolia (read): trunks are typically 0.3 to 0.9 m in diameter, and trees live about 150 years on average. A stem 0.05 m in radius under its crown that thickens 1.7 mm a year is 0.6 m across, the middle of that range, at 150 years.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: slow, a few centimetres a year; about 1 m at 20 years, 2.5 to 3 m at 50, 4 to 5 m at 90. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: olive green leaves, grey-brown dead leaves on the branches, creamy flower clusters; the leaves and the old trunk's dark grey-brown bark set again against iNaturalist photographs (imagekit) on 2026-10-27, from the colour of sunlit rosettes and trunks: the leaves were bluish green and the bark a pale tan, where the trunks in the photographs are near black. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): six greenish-white tepals in two whorls, six stamens and a superior pistil of three carpels, from the characters of Asparagaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

traits.rosette.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 226, Yucca brevifolia: rosette terminal tufts of short stiff leaves at branch tips.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 226, Yucca brevifolia: inflorescence panicle, terminal, dense, ovoid.
